We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps: (1) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). (2) Doebner modification to form the α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (the C=C-CO-). (3) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine.

Thus retrosynthetic direction: target -> break amide bond to give carboxylic acid and aniline (or amine). Then break the α,β-unsaturated acid to give aldehyde + malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. So retro: the unsaturated acid fragment (C=C-CO-) can be disconnected to aromatic aldehyde (the aryl ring with aldehyde) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). The aldehyde is attached to the phenyl ring that later attaches to sulfonyl group? Wait structure: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl ring (c2) via the double bond: phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline. So the α,β-unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl ring at the β carbon (the double bond). In Doebner, the aldehyde is attached to aromatic ring, then malonic acid gives the unsaturated acid attached at the β carbon (the double bond). So retro: we can disconnect the double bond to give aromatic aldehyde (c2-CHO) and malonic acid.

Thus step 2: break C=C bond to give aldehyde (c2-CHO) and malonic acid.

Step 3: sulfonamide formation: the sulfonamide linking the first phenyl (with methyl) to the second phenyl via sulfonyl group. So retro: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2-Cl) and aniline (the second phenyl with NH2). Actually the sulfonamide is between the first phenyl (with methyl) and the second phenyl (the one bearing the unsaturated amide). The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl (as -NH- linking to sulfonyl). Wait SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2)cc1. So the first phenyl (with methyl) has -NH- attached to sulfonyl group which is attached to second phenyl. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is on the first phenyl (an aniline). So retro: break S-N to give sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl (Ar-SO2-Cl) and aniline (first phenyl with NH2). So we need template for sulfonamide formation (reverse direction). The template we retrieved (id 733) is for sulfonamide formation: forward reaction is Cl-SO2-Ar + Aniline -> sulfonamide. The retro template (retro_smarts) is the reverse: sulfonamide -> Cl-SO2-Ar + Aniline. Good.

Thus we need to construct route JSON: root molecule target, then reaction 1 (amide formation) or order? The guidance says reactions enumerated in order they must be applied (forward). For retrosynthesis we need to list reactions in reverse order? In example they show root molecule with children reaction then precursors. So we need to break target into precursors via reaction nodes. The order of reactions in route should be from target to precursors (i.e., first reaction is the last step in synthesis). So we need three reaction nodes: first (most recent) amide formation, second Doebner modification, third sulfonamide formation.

Thus we need template IDs for each step.

We have template 733 for sulfonamide formation (reverse). For amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine -> amide) we need a template. Search for amide formation. Use search with functional_groups_broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid, formed: amide. Already attempted but got error because "carboxylic acid" not valid; need "aliphatic carboxylic acid". Let's try again.
